title: Private Upgrades: Customer Maintenance Window + Backup + Rollback Comms (Draft Template)
body:
Doc purpose
- Customer-facing message templates for Redwood Private upgrades (VPC + on-prem/air-gapped).
- Covers: how to schedule a maintenance window, what customers should back up, what downtime/impact to expect, and what “rollback” means in practice.
- This is a working draft for beta design partners; tone is intentionally direct and operational.

Owner notes (internal)
- Keep promises conservative; avoid absolute guarantees about “no downtime.”
- If customer has compliance/audit requirements, include the “Audit evidence” addendum.
- For air-gapped customers, always include the “Offline bundle” section.

============================================================
TEMPLATE 1 — Initial notice (recommended: send 7–10 days before)

Subject: Scheduled maintenance: Redwood Private upgrade to {TARGET_VERSION} on {DATE}

Hi {CUSTOMER_NAME},

We’re planning to upgrade your Redwood Private environment from {CURRENT_VERSION} to {TARGET_VERSION}.

Proposed maintenance window
- Date/time: {WINDOW_START} – {WINDOW_END} ({TIMEZONE})
- Expected service impact: {IMPACT_LEVEL} (details below)
- Requested customer on-call contact(s): {CUSTOMER_ONCALL_NAME} / {CUSTOMER_ONCALL_EMAIL} / {CUSTOMER_ONCALL_PHONE}

What’s changing
- Redwood Private platform version: {CURRENT_VERSION} → {TARGET_VERSION}
- Upgrade type: in-place upgrade with preflight checks + automated backup + rollback entry points
- Supported path: we generally recommend N-1 → N upgrades (e.g., {CURRENT_VERSION} → {TARGET_VERSION}). If you are more than one minor version behind, we’ll confirm the supported path and plan with you.

Expected impact / downtime
During the window, you may see:
- Brief control plane interruptions (Console access, admin APIs): typically intermittent during component restarts.
- Data plane impact (inference requests): {DATA_PLANE_IMPACT}

Our current guidance for planning purposes:
- Total window: {WINDOW_DURATION} (recommended)
- Expected “hands-on” upgrade time: {EXPECTED_DURATION}
- Potential request impact: {REQUEST_IMPACT_SUMMARY}

Notes:
- We design upgrades to be safe-by-default and to fail fast during preflight checks (before changes are applied).
- If a rollback is required, timing depends on the stage of the upgrade (details in “Rollback expectations” below).

Pre-upgrade checklist (customer)
Please confirm by {CONFIRM_BY_DATE}:
1) Maintenance window approval
- Confirm the proposed window or suggest alternatives.
- Confirm whether you have a change-management CAB process and if we should align to a specific approval ticket.

2) Backups you should take (customer-owned)
Even though Redwood performs automated backups as part of the upgrade workflow, we strongly recommend customers take (or validate) their own backups/snapshots according to their standards.

Minimum recommended backups prior to starting the window:
- Persistent volumes / storage snapshots for Redwood Private stateful components (per your storage backend)
- Redwood Private database backup (if you manage it) OR confirmation that the in-cluster DB PV snapshot is enabled
- A copy of your current configuration/values:
  - Helm values files (or Terraform variables) used for the current deployment
  - Custom config overrides (if any)
  - TLS certificate material (or references) and rotation process
  - Identity configuration details (OIDC/SAML settings, client IDs, redirect URIs)
- Any customer-managed integration secrets/refs (KMS keys, external secret store paths) 

Optional (recommended for faster recovery):
- Snapshot/backup of your internal container registry / artifact mirror (for on-prem and restricted environments)

3) Capacity / storage headroom
- Ensure sufficient storage headroom for snapshot creation and temporary artifacts.
- If you’ve recently had storage pressure alerts, please let us know so we can validate remediation before the window.

4) Access requirements for Redwood support (if applicable)
- Confirm that Redwood operators will have {ACCESS_METHOD} access during the window (e.g., break-glass SSO group, VPN route, bastion, temporary kubeconfig).

What Redwood will do during the window
High-level steps (operator-led):
1) Preflight validation
- Cluster health checks (Kubernetes readiness), networking/DNS/TLS validation, identity reachability, artifact availability, version compatibility checks, and storage headroom validation.

2) Automated backup capture
- Orchestrate snapshots / logical backups (depending on your environment and configured storage backend), then verify backup completion.

3) Upgrade execution
- Upgrade control plane components first, then data plane components (to minimize request disruption).
- Apply required migrations with guardrails.

4) Post-upgrade verification
- Verify platform health, key endpoints, and basic request flow.
- Confirm version reporting and audit log event emission.

Rollback expectations (what it means, when we use it)
If the upgrade encounters a blocking issue, we will choose the safest path among:
A) Stop before applying changes (no rollback needed)
- If preflight checks fail, the upgrade does not proceed.

B) Roll back to the previous version (rollback invocation)
- If changes have been applied and health checks fail, we can invoke rollback to restore the last known-good version using the recorded upgrade state and rollback hooks.

Important constraints to understand:
- Rollback is designed to be deterministic for supported upgrade paths and common failure modes.
- If the upgrade has already applied certain irreversible data migrations (rare, but possible depending on your version path and environment), rollback may require additional manual steps. If that situation occurs, we will communicate clearly during the window and provide an explicit recovery plan.
- Rollback restores platform services; it does not retroactively “undo” any customer application changes made during the window.

Success criteria (how we’ll declare the upgrade complete)
We will consider the upgrade complete when:
- Platform reports version {TARGET_VERSION}
- Control plane health checks pass
- Data plane inference path is stable (no elevated error rates beyond agreed thresholds)
- Post-upgrade verification checklist is completed and shared

Support + escalation during the window
- Redwood primary contact: {REDWOOD_PRIMARY_NAME} ({REDWOOD_PRIMARY_EMAIL})
- Redwood backup contact: {REDWOOD_BACKUP_NAME} ({REDWOOD_BACKUP_EMAIL})
- Escalation path (if urgent): {ESCALATION_DETAILS}

Please reply with:
1) Approval for {WINDOW_START} – {WINDOW_END} ({TIMEZONE})
2) Your on-call contact(s) for the window
3) Any constraints we should plan for (CAB approvals, blackout dates, change freezes, security requirements)

Thanks,
{SENDER_NAME}
Redwood Inference

============================================================
TEMPLATE 2 — Reminder (recommended: 24–48 hours before)

Subject: Reminder: Redwood Private upgrade window {WINDOW_START} – {WINDOW_END} ({TIMEZONE})

Hi {CUSTOMER_NAME},

Reminder that we’re scheduled to upgrade your Redwood Private environment from {CURRENT_VERSION} to {TARGET_VERSION} during:
- {WINDOW_START} – {WINDOW_END} ({TIMEZONE})

Before we start, please confirm:
- You’ve taken/validated your backups (see prior email)
- Your on-call contact(s) are available: {CUSTOMER_ONCALL_NAME}
- Any final access approvals are complete (VPN/SSO/bastion/kube access)

At the start of the window, we will run preflight checks and will stop immediately if any blocking issues are detected.

Thanks,
{SENDER_NAME}

============================================================
TEMPLATE 3 — Completion note (post-window)

Subject: Completed: Redwood Private upgrade to {TARGET_VERSION}

Hi {CUSTOMER_NAME},

We completed your Redwood Private upgrade to {TARGET_VERSION} on {DATE}.

Summary
- Window: {WINDOW_START} – {WINDOW_END} ({TIMEZONE})
- Outcome: {OUTCOME} (e.g., Successful / Successful with mitigation / Rolled back)
- Customer-visible impact: {IMPACT_SUMMARY}

Verification performed
- Control plane health: {HEALTH_STATUS}
- Data plane request checks: {REQUEST_CHECKS_SUMMARY}
- Version confirmation: {VERSION_CONFIRMATION_DETAILS}

Notes / follow-ups
- {FOLLOWUP_1}
- {FOLLOWUP_2}

If you observed any anomalies after the window, please reply to this thread and include:
- Approximate timestamp(s)
- Request IDs (if available)
- Relevant logs/metrics screenshots

Thanks,
{SENDER_NAME}

============================================================
ADDENDUM A — On-prem / air-gapped environments (include when relevant)

Offline upgrade bundle requirements
- We will provide (or validate) an upgrade bundle for {TARGET_VERSION} including required images/charts/manifests.
- Please ensure:
  - Bundle is present in the agreed location: {BUNDLE_LOCATION}
  - Checksums/signatures can be validated in your environment
  - Offline registry / artifact mirror endpoints are reachable from the cluster

Common causes of delay in air-gapped upgrades
- Missing images in offline registry
- Bundle verification errors (checksum/signature mismatch)
- DNS/TLS issues when reaching internal artifact endpoints

============================================================
ADDENDUM B — Audit evidence (regulated environments)

During the upgrade, Redwood can provide artifacts such as:
- Upgrade plan summary (what steps were intended)
- Preflight check results (pass/warn/fail with timestamps)
- Backup completion status
- Upgrade start/stop timestamps
- Rollback invocation timestamp (if applicable)

If you need retention/forwarding to your SIEM, confirm:
- Required fields (customer environment ID, operator identity, timestamps)
- Preferred export format and destination

============================================================
FAQ (optional to include as a final section or separate doc)

Q: Can we do the upgrade with zero downtime?
A: We minimize disruption, but exact downtime depends on cluster topology and the set of changes in {TARGET_VERSION}. Plan for impact within the maintenance window.

Q: What if preflight checks fail?
A: We stop before applying changes and provide a remediation checklist. We can reschedule once the issue is resolved.

Q: What exactly is rolled back?
A: Platform components are rolled back to the prior known-good version using the recorded upgrade state and rollback hooks. In rare cases where irreversible migrations have already been applied, additional manual steps may be required; we will communicate that clearly if it occurs.

Q: Can we postpone?
A: Yes—please propose alternative windows and note any change freezes/blackouts.
